_README: DIALECT-NORMALIZATION RE-MEASUREMENT under the testbench-dialect-normalization spec,
task 18.1.
Identical arms/problems/n=3/caps/limits/seed/temperature/concurrency to
stage1-screen-repair-v1, which is the campaign this one is compared against. The ONLY
difference is the Dialect_Normalizer now running ahead of the testbench precheck
(NORMALIZER_VERSION 4) and the repair-path retirement that came with it
(TESTBENCH_REPAIR_POLICY_VERSION 2).
Version 4 arrived after this config was authored: on top of the version-3 transform it
PRESERVES the signed-base marker in a rewritten sized literal (16'sd-1 -> (-16'sd1), not
the unsigned (-16'd1), which a vvp run showed compares against zero the other way), and
it REPORTS a #-preceded literal's decline under rewrite-context-not-established instead
of declining it silently and undercounting the class.
WHAT IT IS SCORED AGAINST. stage1-screen-repair-v1 recorded 48 precheck-arm samples with
0 accepted repairs. 45 of those 48 captured a `syntax error` in control-stderr.txt and
are therefore the classified population.
PREDICTED EFFECT: 28 of 45 - 25 of 29 unnamed-begin-declaration, plus 3 of 7
malformed-sized-literal, plus 0 of 4 prose-as-statement. The 28 is MEASURED on the 40
committed fixtures against the real toolchain rather than predicted, and that is what
makes it usable as a prediction: a campaign recovering materially fewer than 28 is a REAL
DISCREPANCY worth investigating - a rule that stopped firing, a dialect shape the
fixtures do not cover, or a difference between the campaign's compile path and the
fixture suite's - rather than noise.
KNOWN RESIDUE this run will also show, so it is not misread as failure: 4
unnamed-begin-declaration declines (3 unbalanced-block, 1 declaration-not-relocatable), 4
malformed-sized-literal declines (value-not-determinable), and all 4 prose-as-statement,
which are reported and never rewritten.
TWO SUPERSEDED FIGURES, recorded so nobody restores them. An earlier 32 of 48 rested on
an unverified hand count. A later 36 of 45 assumed ALL 29 plus ALL 7 would be fixed and
was optimistic by 8: its 45-sample denominator and its three class sizes were derived
from the real artifacts, but its 36 numerator was never measured. Do not restate 36 as
measured and do not predict against either figure.
EXPLICIT NON-GOAL: this says NOTHING about the 229 TESTBENCH_FAILED_REFERENCE samples. It
addresses build failures only, which is Council B's stated condition on this spec's
scope. A drop in build failures is not progress on reference-failing testbenches.
A fresh outputDir is REQUIRED, not a preference: v11-and-earlier results records are
refused wholesale by RESULTS_SCHEMA_VERSION 12, so this cannot resume or append into
.eval-runs/stage1-screen-repair-v1.
THE CONFIG HASH WILL NOT MATCH the one recorded in stage1-screen-repair-v1's manifest,
and that is correct and expected: NORMALIZER_VERSION is now 4 and
TESTBENCH_REPAIR_POLICY_VERSION is now 2, and config-identity.ts folds both into the
canonical JSON directly from the running code. This is deliberately a DIFFERENT
experiment whose samples must NEVER pool with the old ones. The comparison is done by
reading the two summaries side by side, never by pooling records. Note also that runName
and outputDir ARE identity-bearing (config-identity.ts excludes only captureArtifacts),
so the rename alone would move the hash even if no version had changed - which is
harmless here precisely because nothing pools.
node --env-file=.env app/eval/dist/sweep/cli.js --config app/eval/sweep/sweep.config.stage1-screen-dialect-v1.json
The credential NEVER goes in this file. It comes from the environment (.env).
prices is empty by design, so the run reports token floors and UNKNOWN dollars rather
than a fabricated cost.
_problems: The same 15 designs as sweep.config.tbslice.json, spanning arithmetic, control, memory,
and miscellaneous, none of them Stage 0 quarantined. Reused deliberately: we already
have a kimi-k2.5 reading on this exact set (tbslice-v2), so that arm doubles as a
sanity check that this screen reproduces a known result.
_caps: The SAME student-session caps a real student gets. Never widened for eval.
_concurrency: 3, not 1. The two previous wide attempts (instrument-calibration, stage1-screening) both
died to a rate-limit burst, so this stays well under the host limit while still cutting
a ~2h serial run to well under an hour. The breaker and backoff handle the rest.
_killSwitch: 6h wall and 550 samples: 495 planned (11 arms x 15 problems x 3) plus headroom. Stops
DISPATCH at a sample boundary, so everything recorded stays on disk and resumable.
_sampling: n=3, NOT n=1, and this was measured rather than assumed.
stage1-screen-v1 ran this same config at n=1 and was ABANDONED after 15 samples, because
the kimi-k2.5 arm disagreed with the tbslice-v2 run on 3 of its first 10 problems - all
three flipping verified -> instrument-refused on identical inputs at temperature 0.
The artifacts name the cause: instrument_control_tb.v syntax errors / Malformed statement,
i.e. the MODEL emitted different, invalid testbench Verilog on the second run. Not a
timeout, not sandbox contention - a genuinely stochastic generator. temperature 0 and a
fixed seed are hints to a hosted endpoint, never a guarantee.
So n=1 cannot rank models: a model could place last on variance alone. n=3 gives pass@1
and pass@3 plus a per-arm spread to read the noise floor off. .eval-runs/stage1-screen-v1
is kept as the evidence for this choice.
